camera.elevation: street level (LoC summary: "street level view, from an oblique angle")
camera.basis: South portico (pediment) on the right, west flank colonnade receding left => viewer in the SW quadrant of the church, looking NE. Church axis from OSM way 54180046 (Nominatim): facade faces ~207° (towards rue Royale). Ratio of drawn flank (~190 px) to facade (~250 px) vs real lengths (~128 m vs ~43 m, computed from OSM polygon) implies line of sight ~15-30° off the church axis. Tree-lined street at right horizon interpreted (not verified) as the start of the Grands Boulevards. Lithograph perspective may be constructed by the draughtsman; radius reflects this.

pairs.reasons: Panoramax GPS lies on the rue Royale axis ~182 m from the facade, inside the estimated camera zone; church centred in both. Caveats: modern file is a 360° equirectangular panorama (church ~2% of width) — a viewer must render a ~20-25° perspective crop at heading ~26° to compare visually; historic distance estimate depends on an assumed lens (±70 m).
Same axis and direction (21° vs ~26°), but taken ~35 m from the portico instead of ~150-230 m; wide-angle low viewpoint; flanking buildings of rue Royale not in frame.

Same SW quadrant and same visible faces (south portico + west colonnade, same left/right arrangement). But: 360° panorama, trees partly mask the colonnade, Benoist perspective is drawn (possibly constructed) and his exact standpoint is uncertain (±60 m).
Same quadrant/orientation; Baldus is closer and at a lower, more lateral angle; panorama projection.
Both street-level from the SW, same faces visible; Baldus slightly more westerly and closer. Good pair for a lithograph-vs-photograph comparison.
Photochrom is taken from an elevated position (est. 15-25 m); no elevated modern photo found in Panoramax.

targets.instructions: South-west part of Place de la Madeleine, where rue Royale opens onto the square; stand on the pavement so that the south portico (pediment) is on the right and the west colonnade recedes to the left; eye level; 35-50 mm (35mm-equivalent) lens, camera level (no tilt) to keep columns vertical; whole building in frame.
Requires an upper-floor window/roof (~15-25 m) on the SW side of the square — private property; only with owner permission. Not a public task.

Middle of rue Royale near the rue Saint-Honoré crossing (traffic! use the central refuge/pedestrian crossing only); facade centred; ~50-70 mm equivalent. A flat (non-360) modern photo from here was not found in Panoramax on 2026-11-07.
